newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk military defends its warning to Islamists.
newsitem.headline: Turk military defends its warning to Islamists.

text.p: Turkey's powerful military issued at statement on Saturday defending its warning to the country's Islamist-led government, saying that it was acting within the constitution.

"The Turkish armed forces are a constitutional institution, their duties and responsibilities are determined by law," said the statement from the General Secretariat of the Chiefs of Staff, quoted by the semi-official Anatolian news agency.
A close aide of Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan called in comments published on Friday for a general election to gain a stronger mandate in the government's tussle with the military.
"When it comes to giving an account to the people the soldiers' attitude will change," the aide, Abdullah Gul, said.

"It is very saddening that sometimes the Turkish armed forces become the subject of political polemic. The National Security Council (MGK) is a legal platform. The commanders, as members of the MGK, here freely bring out their views and ideas," the military statement said.
The military-dominated council last weekend ordered Erbakan's Islamist-led government to stamp out Islamist activity which it says endangers Turkey secular constitution.

After the council's warning, Erbakan pleaded that the army was subverting democracy, while coalition partner Tansu Ciller was quoted as saying she would ask for a parliamentary debate into planned anti-Islamist measures.
The secularist army fears Erbakan's Welfare Party could pave the way to turning NATO-member Turkey into an Islamist state.
